$comment: VAPP-85: the ONE declarative macro table. A macro component (core.catalog.json `kind: macro`) expands into this template before painting; the TS reference expander (src/macros.ts) and the Rust core apply the same table and fixtures/catalog-macros.json locks the output. Template node = { part, component, props?, style?, children?, slots?, $if?, $any?, $each?, $as?, $on?, $context?, $set?, $recipe?, $a11y? }. Values: `"{props.x}"` alone = the raw prop (a data BINDING passes through untouched, so two-way binding survives); `"{props.x|fallback}"` = with a default; `{…}` inside a longer string interpolates; `{id}` = the macro node's id; `{len(props.rows)}` = an array length; `{range(props.max|5)}` = the indexes 0..n-1 (for `$each`; VAPP-290: `range(3)` = a literal count); `{index}` = the current $each index; `{!path}` negates. Value objects: $map {from, cases, default}, $cond [condition, then, else], $eq [a, b] (a number equals a string spelling it), $lt [a, b], $add [a, b], $sub [a, b], $clamp [value, min, max] (a missing bound does not clamp), $percent [value, max] (→ "N%"), $coalesce [a, b, …], $text value (→ the value as a string, absent when missing), $not condition, $fill [template, {name: value}] (ALWAYS emits the core `fill` call: the template is usually a `$string.<id>` sentence with `{name}` placeholders the surface's string table resolves at bind time). Object KEYS interpolate too (`"@media (max-width: $breakpoint.{props.collapseBelow|md})"`). `$if` = a condition or an array of conditions (all must hold); `$any` = an array where one must hold. `$each` repeats a part per item of an array (`$as` names the item, default `item`). Children: `"$children"` splices the author's children, `"$slot:name"` splices an author slot in place; `slots: {"trigger": "$slot:trigger"}` copies an author slot, `slots: {"footer": {template node}}` builds one as a part. `$on: {"press": "change"}` routes the author's `on.change` handler to this part's `press` (merging `$context` into an event action's context); without `$on` the author's `on` map stays on the root. `$set: {"press": {"prop": "open", "value": "{!props.open}"}}` = TWO-WAY BINDING (round 1): when the author's `props.open` is a data binding `{"@path"}`, this part's `press` action also carries `functionCall: {"@call": "set", args: {path, value}}` (the value evaluated like any template value, so usually a call), key order `event` then `functionCall`; a literal prop adds nothing (the host owns the state through the routed event); when the author's routed handler is itself a FUNCTION (an Action carries one), it wins, no `set` is added and the reducer reports an issue. `$a11y: {role, label, description, level, expanded, current, selected, pressed, checked, valueNow, valueMin, valueMax, hidden, autoFocus}` = the part's ACCESSIBILITY (docs/round-1-contract.md §6): evaluated like props (a bound input emits a call) into the expanded node's `accessibility`; `role` is one of catalog/a11y.json `roles`; on the root the author's `accessibility` label/description win. Ids: the root keeps the author's id, parts get `<id>.<part>` and `<id>.<part>.<index>` under `$each`. Every expanded node carries `recipe: {macro, part, props}` where props = `recipeProps` evaluated from the author's props (+ a part's `$recipe`); the THEME (VAPP-92) keys its visual recipes on that, so nothing here states a colour, a border or a font — only structure and token-named spacing, radius and control heights. VAPP-163: the expansion ROOT's recipe also carries `authored` = the top-level keys of the style written ON the macro node (condition blocks count as one key), SORTED, omitted when none; painters apply native recipe < node style < part recipe < those authored keys, so an author's colour or size on a Heading/Badge beats the theme's part recipe while the template's own structure does not (only the author's keys count: a macro node an outer template drew passes on just its root's `authored`, never template style). Macros may use other macros (Row → TreeGuides); expansion recurses until every node is native (innermost recipe wins). ROUND 1 (docs/round-1-contract.md §1, BOUND INPUTS): when an expression input is a data binding `{"@path"}` or a function call `{"@call"}`, the expander does NOT evaluate — it EMITS an A2UI function call the renderer evaluates at bind time, over the core functions: interpolation → concat, `|fallback` → fallback (as an operand; a whole-string MEMBER of props/style/context passes the binding itself through, so two-way binding survives), `!` → not, len → len, $map → map, $cond → cond, $eq → eq, $lt → lt, $add → add, $sub → sub, $percent → percent, $text → text, $coalesce → coalesce, $not → not; a `$if`/`$any` whose conditions are bound emits the part WITH `visible` = the bound condition (`and{values}` over several bound `$if`s, `or{values}` over several bound `$any`s; literal conditions still decide at expansion; VAPP-289 (round 9 §6.7): a bound condition operand (`$if`, `$any`, `$not`, `{!…}`) that is NOT boolean-typed (a prop whose catalog type is not `boolean`, or a call that does not return a boolean) is wrapped as `{"@call": "cond", "args": {"if": <operand>, "then": true, "else": false}}` so presence semantics survive A2UI 1.0's boolean coercion); `$each` over a bound array emits nothing (use List with a template); a `$recipe` value may therefore be a call too (renderers resolve recipe props like props). RESPONSIVE PROPS: an author prop `{base, sm?, md?, lg?, xl?}` on a `responsive` prop is evaluated per breakpoint: a part's style is computed with the `base` values, then once per breakpoint named (ascending sm<md<lg<xl, each key inheriting the last smaller one) and every key that changed lands in a `"@media (min-width: $breakpoint.<bp>)"` block of that part; props and conditions see the `base` value. Strings of the form `$string.<id>` (catalog/strings.json) are built-in UI copy the renderer shows in the surface locale. Round 3 (VAPP-102): AFTER the table is applied the core runs ONE post-expansion pass, src/tree-guides.ts applyTreeGuides (Rust: tree_guides::apply): over every node's children in order, each Row root (`recipe.macro` Row, part root) contributes its numeric `recipe.props.depth` (anything else counts as depth 0 and ends every subtree), the ×4 treeGuides rule (elbow at depth-1, tee while a later sibling follows, pass-through for every ancestor level that continues) fills the Row's `guides` part (a TreeGuides) with `elbowAt`/`tee`/`passThrough`; fixtures/tree-guides.json locks the rule, catalog-macros.json the filled trees. EXP-1495 (docs/round-6-contract.md): Outline (the anchor list) and Mosaic (the wide picture group) are macros over Box/Text/Image. eApps U3 (VAPP-232): `$template: {path, key?, item}` = a DATA TEMPLATE part: `path` (evaluated like any value; a data pointer, absolute or relative inside an outer template) names the array the part renders `item` once per entry of, keyed by `key`; the part gets `template: {component: <part id>.<item part>, path, key?}` and the item node (expanded like the root, tree guides filled) is lifted into the reducer's `templates` after the authored ones, in build order (the root's first); an empty or non-string path builds nothing. The item reads its entry through RELATIVE bindings (`{"@path": "date"}`), and a routed `$on` handler runs in the item's scope, so an author's `{"@path": "date"}` reads the pressed day. Calendar and Timeline (catalog `kind: macro`) are built this way over a records calendar view; fixtures/template-items.json `reduce` (macro-template-*) locks the lifted items. VAPP-250: `Timeline` on the phone form factor scrolls as ONE scroller: its root takes `overflowX: auto`, the bands row, the columns row and the rows are at least the label column (96) + 72 per column wide (the literals below, no renderer reads them; `@media (form-factor: phone)` only, wide keeps the fr columns), and the label column and its header corners are `position: sticky` at `insetInlineStart: 0` on the surface background so they stay on screen while the weeks move. The row heights need no matching: label and track are still one flex row. #VAPP-277 (docs/round-7-contract.md): a def's `$pass: [{slot, component, $if?, props}]` runs BEFORE the macro's author slots expand (expansion is bottom-up, so no template can restyle its slot's nodes): when `$if` holds (literal, in the macro's context) every `component` node in the author's `slot` subtree (a nested node of the same macro ends the walk) takes `props`, evaluated like any value (a whole-string `{props.x}` passes a binding itself), never over a prop its author set. A template child `{"$slot": name, "$if"?, "$any"?}` splices an author slot only while its conditions hold (bound: with `visible`, and-ed with the slot's own). Sidebar `rail` hands its `collapsed` to the sidebar's Rows and Sections as an internal `rail` (Rows also `railSide`: `end`, `start` for a right Sidebar): a rail Row is a `$control.buttonIcon` square, its text parts and slots drop, a `tip` Tooltip (the title, on the logical `railSide`, mirrored under rtl) wraps the `tile` (icon + the `meta` count as a `badge` on its top-end corner) and the root's accessible name is the title (`, <meta>` when set); a rail Section draws a `rule` (Separator) instead of its header and always shows its body. #VAPP-284 (docs/round-7-contract.md): a def may carry `alternatives` [{$if, root}]: the first whose `$if` holds AT EXPANSION (a bound condition never picks one) replaces `root`, its root part keeping the author's id whatever it is named; the conditions (and every value of the expansion) see `{childCount}` = the author's children. A `$on` value may be `{event, context}` = that macro event with its OWN context instead of the part's `$context` (a part routing two events, Row's head: `press` plain, `toggle` with `{open}`). Row with children = a foldable parent: root part `group` (column) → `head` (a nested Row with the author's props, aria-expanded, `toggle` → change {open: !open} + the two-way set; a pressable author Row keeps `press` and gets the `fold` button (press/toggle → change) holding `foldIcon` in its trailing slot; a plain one folds on the head press, `foldIcon` decorative) → `children` (only when `open`: role group, indented `$spacing.lg`, the author's children). The chevron is `ui-chevron-right` turned 90° by the `open` recipe (rtl mirrors it first, so it points left, then down). On a rail (a collapsed rail Sidebar passes `rail` to every Row under it, children included) a foldable parent keeps its `head` tile and its children always follow as tiles, unindented, whatever `open` (as a rail Section shows a closed body). #VAPP-285 (docs/round-7-contract.md): `{treeRows(props)}` = a Tree's flat rows (src/tree.ts treeRows: depth-first over `props.items`, under `props.expanded`; a bound `expanded` emits every row with `expr` calls), the `$each` of its `row` part (a Row per node, depth → the tree guides). `$on` / `$set` KEYS and a routed `event` may interpolate (`{node.toggleOn}`); an empty one routes and writes nothing (a Tree row routes per kind). A rail Sidebar also passes `rail`/`railSide` to a Tree: every row shows as a rail tile (role button, depth 0, no level/expanded, its leading fold glyph dropped) whatever `expanded`, the root a group (treeRows(props) reads `rail`). Round 8 (docs/round-8-contract.md): Progress gains a `header` row (`label` growing, `value` = `valueText` at its end, muted) shown when either is set, and a `detail` caption under the track (also the bar's accessible description); the theme colours `value` and `detail` (neutral: mutedForeground) and painters set `value` in tabular numerals (so does Meter's `value`, the same counting text). Stepper gains `collapse` through `alternatives` (a LITERAL collapse; never = the root as before): `always` = a list holding ONE `line` (`$each` step `$if` current: `$string.stepCompact` filled with step = current + 1, total, label); `auto` = a column holding the full Stepper as the `full` part and that list as the `compact` part, switched by the `@container (max-width: $breakpoint.sm)` style condition (style.json: matched against the width of the node's PARENT box, here the Stepper's own root, so the Stepper collapses when ITS box is narrower than sm, wherever it sits).
